text:
kevin: Heads-up — interruption rates in us-east1 have climbed ~3x over the last 24h for our transient GPU pools. Seeing more requeues and tail latency when jobs get bounced to cold hosts. Should we shift critical inference pools to capacity-first sourcing and keep price-first for background training? :thinking:

jana: I would split by SLO. Critical inferencers -> capacity-aware (prefer non-preemptible or high-capacity zones). Batch jobs -> price-optimized. Also recommend a tiny warm buffer for critical pools (5-10%) so we avoid cold starts on eviction.

li: Agree on SLO-based split. One nuance: capacity-first ≠ always highest price. We can do capacity-weighted bidding: prefer pools with stable historical availability even if slightly pricier. Also throttle durable work to cheaper types (T4/RTXA5000) and keep latency-sensitive on A100s with capacity bias.

marta: Pushed a quick cost/regression calc yesterday — shifting 20% of critical traffic to capacity-pref reduced interruption-driven retries by ~60% but increased unit cost ~12%. If we accept that delta for SLOs it pays off. I can share the calc.

kevin: Nice. Two operational questions: (1) how to implement dynamic rule switching (time-of-day or market-signal triggered); (2) how do we do graceful preempt handling to avoid user-visible errors?

jana: For (1) we can add a market-signal agent that watches per-region interruption rate and average price. Rules: if interruption_rate > 1.5x baseline OR median_price spike > 25% -> flip to capacity_preference for selected pools. For (2) use short-lived reservations + local checkpointing + immediate routing to fallback pool.

li: Implementation sketch for market agent (pseudo):
```
watchers:
  - metric: spot_eviction_rate
    window: 10m
    threshold: 1.5
actions:
  - set_mode: capacity_first
    scope: inference-critical
    hold_for: 30m
```
Keep hold_for to avoid oscillation. Also add hysteresis and backoff.

marta: Also consider a mixed-capacity pool pattern: maintain a small % of instances as reserved/dedicated for blips, backed by larger spot footprint. When spot interruptions spike, we failover X tokens/sec to the reserved slice. That avoids capacity collapse.

kevin: How big should that reserved slice be? 5%? 10%?

marta: Based on current variance I'd start with 7% for inference-critical, 3% for medium batch, 0% for low-priority async. We'll tune after a week.

ops-bot: [incident] evictions detected: us-east1-gpu-pool - 2026-03-17T21:13:24Z - 42 hosts reclaimed.

li: Ops-bot posted — this matches the spike window. We should run a short simulation to estimate failover latency and token loss with 7% reserved. I can spin up a job to simulate 1h of churn.

jana: Also add a bid-floor policy to avoid hammered auctions (don’t go below 30% of on-demand for critical pools). For price-first pools keep aggressive floor at 10-15%.

kevin: Good idea. Any thoughts on multi-region spill? If us-east is hammered we should spill to us-west or eu-west before hitting dreaded on-demand. But latency to users matters for some inference.

li: Use policy routing: prefer same-region capacity-first, then cross-region capacity-first (with region-aware latency budget), then price-first same-region, finally price-first cross-region. We can encode region latency budgets per service.

marta: Example fleet policy snippet (for fleet manager):
```
policy:
  inference-critical:
    prefer: [capacity_score, latency_budget]
    reserved_pct: 7
    bid_floor_pct: 30
    fallback_sequence: [same-region-capacity, cross-region-capacity, same-region-price, cross-region-price]
```
This is intentionally simple; we'll expand parameters.

kevin: Ops checklist for rollout: 1) implement market agent + hysteresis, 2) add reserved slices to fleet config, 3) bid-floor enforcement, 4) simulation job to validate, 5) gradual rollout via canary. Can someone take 1-3?

li: I'll take 1 and 4 (market agent + sim).

jana: I'll handle 2 and 3 (reserved slices + bid floors) and prepare canary plan.

marta: I'll own the cost/regression dashboard and post a week-over-week report.

kevin: Perfect. Let's aim to canary this in us-east1 next Tues. Please add short PRs and a doc in eng-infra runbook about how to revert. :rocket:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary in us-east1 on 2026-03-24 02:00 UTC (auto-created by kevin).

li: Quick note — ensure autoscaler cooldown is increased during canary to avoid premature scale-downs during churn.

jana: Noted. I'll add cooldown to canary config.

kevin: Thanks all. If anyone sees anomalies during the canary ping #oncall and @kevin.

marta: :thumbsup:
